body:
## Purpose

Follow the maintainer-accepted declaration direction in #603 / PR #609 with a narrow real-package typing proof. The maintainer approved the two test seams below before tests.

Accepted direction: separate Python default/default_factory and SQL server_default parameters on existing storage constructors; preserve Col/GenCol, Pending/Row and the explicit Row witness. Repeated default=PENDING_GENERATION is an accepted cost. No wrapper, required=True workaround, duplicate capability claim or generated per-model constructors.

## Confirmed seams

1. Public model declaration/construction: required versus optional inputs, explicit overrides, rejected wrong values, exact Pending/Row field types.
2. Public query-result typing: selected fields and whole-model results retain the expected types.

Anchor cases:

```python
state: db.Col[str] = db.Text(default="draft", server_default="queued")
state: db.Col[str] = db.Text(server_default="queued")
state: db.GenCol[str] = db.Text(
    default=db.PENDING_GENERATION, server_default="queued",
)
```

Cases are separate fields/models, not duplicate declarations. Cover Python factories and appropriate negative controls incrementally as the core evidence permits.

## Method and limits

Use real package declarations copied to a temporary research overlay; no toy replacement Model/Col interfaces, consumer Any/casts/suppression, per-model generated constructors or dependency changes. First record a failing consumer check, then minimally change the copied package annotations for one vertical slice at a time. Verify imported consumers with exact diagnostics/result types. Audit the copied package too and report any remaining errors or accepted false claims honestly.

No production implementation, runtime model/constructor execution, SQL default/DDL checks, backend execution, broader nullability-policy selection, or migration plan. This proves static behavior only; constructor acceptance means checker acceptance, not executed runtime behavior. Do not merge #607 or #609, close umbrella issues, or start production changes. Deliver replayable tests, report and research PR against main; no merge without authorization.

comments.body:
Claiming #610 for continuing session `da58eec6-bf55-4414-99f3-e87a3ee3bee5`, branch `research/split-default-declarations`, from fetched origin/main `5f4dd8189c529a99713b629a71e60088c6974204`.

Assignment verified before investigation/baseline. The maintainer explicitly confirmed the declaration/construction and public query-result typing seams. Isolated real-package static overlay only; no production/runtime/database changes or new declaration alternatives. Red/green slices, exact consumer results/negative controls, and an honest package-wide audit.

Static proof delivered in **draft PR #611**. The accepted declaration forms pass on real-package imports for both SQLite and MariaDB with only an independent optional server_default argument added to copied Text signatures. No wrappers, required=True workaround, callable intersections, new descriptor coordinates or generated per-model constructors.

The 10 focused checks cover the unmodified rejection, clean anchor, paired positive/negative declaration/construction and public query-result typing. There are 50 rejected negative diagnostic sites across both modified backends; SQL fallbacks do not make inputs optional, defaultless GenCol stays required, explicit pending permits omission, and Row/scalar query results exclude pending markers. Bad Python defaults/factories and caller values remain rejected. The entire copied package also passes ty with zero diagnostics; an independent read-only audit replayed all 10 checks without finding consequential gaps.

Limits are important: copied bodies ignore server_default and are never imported/executed. This establishes static feasibility, not runtime defaults, metadata/DDL, INSERT omission, database behavior or Pydantic integration. Legacy default-marker overloads remain in the copy, and only Text plus listed consumers are covered. No production/dependency changes or backend execution occurred.

Replayable report and evidence: `research/split_defaults_610/README.md`; harness: `tests/experimental/test_split_defaults_610.py`. Repository ty/lint/format, whitespace and local report links pass.

Proposed next question—not started—is the remaining default/nullability contract and legacy-marker migration behavior before runtime implementation. Pending-marker repetition is accepted, not a blocker to reopen. #610 and #603 remain open for review; #611 remains draft, and #607/#609 are not merged by this work.

title: Prove split defaults with explicit pending in real-package declarations
